extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and policymakers interested in labor policy, Congress, labor and management leaders
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing President Truman's message to Congress on labor problems, including proposed legislation and procedures (fact-finding boards, cooling-off periods) to prevent large industrial stoppages. Focuses on recommendations, reactions from unions and employers, and procedural details for implementing boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fact-finding boards for important nation-wide disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: A law setting up machinery naming fact-finding boards to prevent work stoppages in important, nation-wide labor disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President recommends adopting principles underlying the Railway Labor Act for wide-spread industries (steel, automobiles, aviation, mining, oil, utilities, communications, etc.), though the list is not exclusive. The general pattern is not intended for small industries or small local disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger: Secretary of Labor certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon certification by the Secretary of Labor that a dispute continues despite his efforts and that work in the affected industry would vitally affect the public interest, the President or his duly authorized agent should be empowered to appoint a fact-finding board within five days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification by the Secretary of Labor is the statutory trigger for appointing the board; the appointment should occur within five days after that certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and investigatory powers of the fact-finding board
rubrics_metrics.description: The board should be composed of three or more outstanding citizens and should be directed to make a thorough investigation of all relevant facts; it should have full power to subpoena individuals and records and be authorized to call upon any Government agency for information or assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should be outstanding citizens; investigators must be able to subpoena witnesses and records and request agency assistance to ensure a full inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report timing and content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The board should make its report within twenty days, unless the date is extended by agreement of the parties with the approval of the President. The report should include a finding of the facts and such recommendations as the board deems appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard report period is twenty days; extensions are allowed only by party agreement and Presidential approval. Reports must include factual findings and recommended actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary prohibition on strikes/lockouts during proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be unlawful to call a strike or lockout, or to make any change in rates of pay, hours or working conditions, or in the established practices in effect prior to the time the dispute arose, during the five days after certification, while the fact-finding board is deliberating, and for five days thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President's proposal envisions a 30-day total 'cooling-off' structure: five days after certification, 20 days for the board's deliberation, and five additional days. No unilateral changes in pay/hours/practices are permitted in that interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-binding nature of board findings but public transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties would not be legally bound to accept the findings or follow the recommendations of the fact-finding board, but the general public would know all the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although recommendations are advisory (not enforceable), publication of findings is expected to exert public pressure to accept them in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit scope to disputes vitally affecting public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation should cover only such stoppages of work as the Secretary of Labor would certify as vitally affecting the public interest; it is not intended for small, local, or inconsequential disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective is to cover wide-spread interruptions that could cripple reconversion and national production; small local disputes should remain outside this machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration for seasonal industries
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislation should pay particular attention to the needs of seasonal industries so that the so-called 'cooling-off periods' can be arranged in those industries in a manner which will not subject labor to an undue disadvantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooling-off timelines and restrictions should be adapted so seasonal work is not unfairly harmed by timing of delays or mandatory waiting periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid measures that stifle collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation which would stifle full freedom of collective bargaining on either side would be a backward step which the American people would not tolerate; the government should not adopt repressive or coercive measures against either side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must balance preventing crippling strikes with preserving free labor and private enterprise; do not undermine core bargaining freedoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Railway Labor Act emergency-board model as precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: For industries where a stoppage would vitally affect the public interest, appointment of a fact-finding board similar to the emergency board under the Railway Labor Act is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Railway Labor Act emergency-board procedures are presented as an effective, fair general pattern for large, nationwide industries, though not universally applicable to small disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential investigators' subpoena authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Presidential investigators, acting as fact-finders, would have the power to subpoena individuals and records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The White House proposal would give investigators statutory power to compel testimony and documents to support thorough fact-finding.
